title: Permutation in String
spaceBreakdown:
- vector<int> cnt(26): fixed size → O(1)  
- loop indices and temporary bool: O(1)  
- not counted: input strings, returned bool
approach:
A permutation of `s1` has exactly the same character frequencies as `s1`.  
Slide a window of length |s1| over `s2` and keep a 26‑element frequency array that is updated when the window moves.  
If at any position the array is all zeros, the current window is a permutation, so return true.
hints:
If we look at every consecutive substring of `s2` whose length equals `s1`, what must be identical between that substring and `s1`?  
`s1` and `s2` consist only of lowercase English letters.

Use an array of size 26 to store character counts.  
Example: for `s1 = "ab"` the array becomes `[1,1,0,…]`; after processing the window `"ba"` in `s2` it returns to all zeros.

```
if |s1| > |s2| return false
cnt = frequency of s1
for i = 0 … |s2|-1
    decrement cnt[s2[i]]
    if i >= |s1|   increment cnt[s2[i-|s1|]]
    if all cnt entries are 0 return true
return false
```

**s1 longer than s2** - `s1` cannot fit inside `s2`.  
`Input: "abcd","abc"` → `Expected: false`  
⚠️ Bug: returning true when the loop never forms a full window → returns true  

**All characters identical** - many repeated letters.  
`Input: "aaa","aaaaa"` → `Expected: true`  
⚠️ Bug: using a `set<char>` instead of counts → returns false  

**Missing permutation** - no window matches.  
`Input: "ab","eidboaoo"` → `Expected: false`  
⚠️ Bug: forgetting to remove the leftmost character when the window slides → returns false  

**Valid permutation at the end** - window reaches the last position.  
`Input: "ab","eidbaooo"` → `Expected: true`  
⚠️ Bug: stopping the scan one step early (i < |s2|-|s1|) → returns false

followUps.q: What if the strings may contain any Unicode characters instead of only lowercase English letters?
followUps.a: Replace the fixed 26‑element array with an unordered_map<char,int> to store frequencies. The algorithm stays linear, O(n) time, and uses O(k) extra space where k is the number of distinct characters in `s1`.

followUps.q: How would you modify the solution to return all start indices of permutations of `s1` in `s2`?
followUps.a: Keep the same sliding‑window logic, but whenever the frequency array becomes all zeros, push the current start index (i‑|s1|+1) into a result vector. Time remains O(n) and extra space is O(1) besides the output list.

followUps.q: Suppose `s2` arrives as a stream and you cannot store the whole string. How can you still solve the problem?
followUps.a: Maintain the same 26‑element count array and a circular buffer of the last |s1| characters from the stream. Update the counts as each new character arrives and the oldest one leaves. This uses O(1) memory and O(n) time.
